text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a software development practice where developers regularly merge their code changes into a shared central repository. The core of CI is the use of automated builds, which compile the new code every time a change is made. After each build, the system automatically runs a series of tests to verify that everything works as expected. This process is controlled by a CI pipeline, a set of automated steps that handle building and testing without manual effort. The main advantage is catching issues early, often within minutes of a change, rather than discovering problems days later. This saves significant time and effort, as bugs are much easier to fix when they are fresh in the developer’s mind. Ultimately, CI helps teams deliver higher-quality software more frequently and with greater confidence.
